transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… I’ve just been worrying all the time. About everything, really—my marriage, work, bills, stuff around the house I’m not keeping up with. I keep feeling like I’m failing as a husband and a father.
When the worrying starts, is it hard for you to stop or control it?

Yeah. It’s… hard to shut it off. I’ll try to just focus on the code in front of me, or tell myself to breathe during a workout, but then one thing leads to another. Like a bad review turns into me losing my job, and then my family being worse off because of me. It gets away from me pretty fast.
How long have you been worrying like this?
Probably around nine months. It got worse when the cloud migration at work ramped up, and… things at home started turning into arguments more regularly.
Do these worries feel mainly tied to the problems at work and the arguments at home, or do you find yourself worrying just as much even when those things aren’t going on?

It’s not just those things, no. They kind of set it off, but then it spreads. I end up worrying about work, money, the house, my marriage… whether I’m letting everyone down. It feels like everything at once.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
I don’t know… not really depressed, I guess. More just worn down. I haven’t really thought of it that way.
Do you often feel restless or keyed up?

Yeah… a lot of the time. I feel kind of wound tight most of the day, like my shoulders are locked up and I’m bracing for something. I’ll catch myself pacing between meetings, or tapping pieces at chess club because sitting still just feels… hard.
Do you get tired easily?
I’m not sure. I mean… I feel worn out a lot, but I don’t know if I’d say I get tired easily exactly.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yeah… I guess so. At work especially. In sprint planning or code reviews I’ll read the same design note three or four times and still miss things. My mind’s kind of… somewhere else, worrying about what I forgot or how the next argument’s going to go.
Has this worrying been interfering with how you function day to day?

Yeah… it has. Work’s been the main place I can’t really hide it. My manager’s started writing down the architecture details I’m missing, which… isn’t great.

And at home I’m not finishing things I start. I’m there, but kind of not there, and then arguments just keep getting worse.
Have you been more irritable than usual?
I don’t know… maybe a little. I haven’t really been keeping track of that.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yeah. Most nights I’m exhausted, but I just… lie there. My head keeps going over work stuff, money, things I said to my wife.

And if I do fall asleep, I’m often up around 3 or 4, already thinking about tomorrow. Then it’s hard to get back to sleep.
Do you often feel muscle tension?

Yeah. Pretty often. My shoulders are kind of… locked up most of the day, like I’m bracing for something.

I also catch myself pacing between meetings, or tapping pieces at chess club. Sitting still just feels hard sometimes.
Do your worries feel out of proportion to what’s actually happening in your life?

Yeah… probably. I mean, I know some of it is normal stuff, but it feels like I can’t stop worrying about all of it at once—my marriage, work, bills, the house things I’m not finishing… whether I’m just not doing enough as a husband or a dad. It feels bigger than it should.
Do you feel this anxiety started mainly because of the problems at work and the arguments at home?
Yeah… I think that’s when it really got going. Maybe about nine months ago, when the cloud migration at work ramped up, and things at home started turning into arguments more regularly.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day?
I don’t know… not most of the day, I don’t think. I’ve been stressed and kind of worn down, but “depressed” feels… I’m not sure.
When work or things at home calm down for a bit, does the worrying still keep going?

Yeah… it does. Even if things quiet down, my head doesn’t really stop. I’ll try to just focus on the code in front of me, or I’ll go work out and try to breathe through it, and then one worry kind of grabs onto another. Before I know it, I’m way ahead—like a bad review turns into losing my job, and then my family being worse off because of me.
If the problems at work and the arguments at home were resolved, do you think the anxiety would mostly go away?

I don’t think so. Maybe it would help, but… the worrying feels bigger than just those two things. It jumps around—my marriage, work, bills, the house stuff I’m behind on. Mostly I keep thinking I’m failing at all of it.
Do you find yourself worrying about many different parts of life, even when there isn’t a specific problem happening at that moment?

Yeah… I do. It’s not just one thing. It’s like everything piles in at once—my marriage, work, bills, stuff around the house I keep putting off. Even when nothing’s actually happening right then, I’m still thinking I’m messing it all up… as a husband, a dad, just… everything.
Do you feel your worrying is more intense than the actual problems would reasonably call for?

Yeah. I think so. It feels… out of proportion a lot of the time. Like I can’t just worry about one thing—I’m worrying about my marriage, work, bills, the house, whether I’m failing as a husband and father. It all gets big fast.
Would you say this anxiety causes you a lot of distress?

Yeah… it does. More than I like admitting. My manager’s started writing down things I missed in architecture details at work, and at home I’m… not really finishing projects, and I’m distracted enough that arguments just keep getting worse.
